objective_text: Understand why computers use binary to represent all forms of data.
Convert between binary, denary and hexadecimal number systems and explain where each is used.
Perform binary addition and logical shifts on 8-bit registers and identify when overflow occurs.
Describe how text is represented using the ASCII and Unicode character sets, and explain why Unicode is needed.
Explain how sound and images are captured as digital data, using sampling, resolution, pixels and colour depth.
Explain why data compression is needed and distinguish lossless from lossy compression methods.
Describe how data is split into packets and reassembled at its destination using packet switching.
Compare serial and parallel transmission, and describe simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex communication.
Describe how IP addresses and MAC addresses are used to route data across a network.
Explain the role of the network interface card and the router when data is transmitted.
Explain how parity checks and checksums are used to detect errors in transmitted data.
Describe the components of the central processing unit and the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
Explain how clock speed, the number of cores and cache size affect the performance of a processor.
Select and justify suitable input and output devices for a given application or scenario.
Compare magnetic, optical and solid-state storage in terms of capacity, speed, durability and cost.
